Taking into account the quality and safety requirements newly imposed by a globalised market, we especially highlight the scientific evidence behind TCM, update the most important milestones and pitfalls, and propose integrity, integration and innovation as key principles for further modernisation of TCM. These principles will serve as foundations for further research and development of TCM, and for its future integration into tomorrow’s medicine.

title: Resolving the amalgam: connecting pedagogical content knowledge, content knowledge and pedagogical knowledge
abstract: This paper concludes the Special Issue (SI) ‘Probing the Amalgam: the relationship between science teachers’ content, pedagogical and pedagogical content knowledge’. We review the five papers (Sorge et al; Gess-Newsome et al; Kind; Pitjeng-Mosabala and Rollnick; and Liepertz and Bronowski) by discussing evidence these present regarding the relationships between content knowledge (CK), pedagogical knowledge (PK) and pedagogical content knowledge (PCK); the development of CK, PK and PCK in novice and experienced secondary science teachers and how CK, PK and/or PCK impact students’ learning. In conclusion, we draw these findings together in offering proposals for future research via reconsideration of Shulman’s amalgam. This includes post-hoc examination of a PCK model known as ‘the Consensus Model’ (Gess-Newsome, [2015]. A model of teacher professional knowledge and skill including PCK: Results of the thinking from the PCK Summit. In A. Berry, P. J. Friedrichsen, & J. Loughran (Eds.), Re-examining Pedagogical Content Knowledge in Science Education (pp. 28–42). New York, NY: Routledge; Neumann, Kind, & Harms [2018]. Probing the amalgam: The relationship between science teachers’ content, pedagogical and pedagogical content knowledge. International Journal of Science Education, 1–15) and presentation of a novel PCK structure based on evidence from the SI studies.

title: Chemistry of personalized solar energy.
abstract: Personalized solar energy (PE) offers a transformative approach to meeting global energy demands by enabling secure, distributed, and carbon-neutral energy access at the individual level. Central to realizing PE is the development of inexpensive, high-density solar energy storage, which necessitates efficient chemical processes for fuel formation, such as HX (X = halide or OH−) and H2O splitting. These reactions require advances in fundamental chemistry, particularly in multielectron transformations, proton-coupled electron transfer, and activation of energy-poor bonds. This paper explores the underlying chemical principles governing these processes, details the challenges associated with catalytic bond activation in solar fuel generation, and outlines discovery pathways for new catalysts inspired by natural photosynthesis. The resulting advances provide a foundation for manufacturable and affordable solar energy storage solutions, positioning chemistry as a key enabler of personalized solar energy for a sustainable future.

title: The physics of optical computing
abstract: This paper examines the renewed interest in optical computing, particularly for special-purpose applications such as neural-network processing, scientific computing, combinatorial optimization, and cryptography. It systematically identifies and analyzes eleven distinct physical features of optics that can be leveraged to achieve computational advantages over traditional electronic processors, emphasizing that the commonly cited speed of light is not the primary differentiator. Instead, potential benefits arise from careful architectural design that combines multiple optical features while mitigating associated pitfalls. The discussion highlights how advances in photonic hardware, the rising computational demands of neural networks, and the limitations of further CMOS scaling have converged to make analog optical computing increasingly viable. The paper also explores the parallels between emerging analog electronic and optical processor architectures, underscoring the importance of robust design to tolerate noise and limited precision inherent to analog computation. Ultimately, it provides a framework for understanding where and how optical computing can outperform electronics for specific tasks, guiding future research and development in this field.

title: Polymer Science and Technology
abstract: The 8th Greek Polymer Society Symposium on Polymer Science and Technology, held in Hersonissos, Crete from 24–29 October 2010, serves as a premier international forum for the presentation and discussion of recent advances in polymer science. The event gathers over 85 leading scientists as invited lecturers and brings together research teams from Greek universities and institutes, fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange among academics, researchers, engineers, and students worldwide. Key topics include polymer synthesis and characterization, properties and applications, self-assembly behavior, biopolymers, colloids, composites, nanocomposites, surface modification, theory, and simulations. The symposium emphasizes the promotion of research cooperation and highlights the global contributions of the Greek polymer community to the field. Poster abstracts are peer-reviewed for scientific merit and novelty, ensuring a high standard of discourse on current challenges and innovations in polymer science and technology.

title: Aquaporins in clinical medicine.
abstract: Aquaporins are a family of membrane water channels, some of which also transport glycerol, that play critical roles in diverse physiological processes including water and salt homeostasis, exocrine fluid secretion, and epidermal hydration. Their dysfunction is implicated in a range of human diseases such as nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, congenital cataracts, neuromyelitis optica, glaucoma, cancer, epilepsy, and obesity. At the cellular level, aquaporins facilitate osmotic water transport essential for transepithelial fluid movement, cell migration, neuroexcitation, and regulate cell proliferation and metabolism through glycerol transport. Genetic mutations and autoimmune targeting of aquaporins can cause or contribute to disease pathogenesis. Advances in understanding aquaporin structure and function have revealed opportunities for the development of novel diagnostics and therapeutics, including small-molecule modulators for treating refractory edema, brain swelling, neuroinflammation, and other conditions. Ongoing research into aquaporin polymorphisms and regulatory mechanisms continues to expand their potential applications in clinical medicine.

title: Facilitators and barriers of herbal medicine use in Accra, Ghana: an inductive exploratory study
abstract: This inductive exploratory qualitative study investigated the facilitators and barriers to herbal medicine use among adults attending a private herbal clinic in Accra, Ghana. Sixteen participants were purposively sampled and interviewed face-to-face, with data analyzed using content analysis. Facilitators identified included convincing information promoting initiation, perceived effectiveness of herbal medicine, personal preference, dissatisfaction with western medicine, and the integration of spirituality. Barriers encompassed negative perceptions and attitudes, poor vending environments, inadequate knowledge among vendors, high costs at reputable clinics, and inconsistent product effectiveness. Participants expressed a desire for national health insurance coverage of herbal medicine to reduce financial burdens. The findings highlight the need for enhanced public education and regulatory monitoring to address negative perceptions and ensure the safety and efficacy of herbal products in Ghana’s healthcare landscape.

title: A Method of Automated Nonparametric Content Analysis for Social Science
abstract: This paper introduces a novel automated nonparametric method for content analysis tailored to social science research, addressing the challenge of estimating category proportions in large corpora of unstructured text. Unlike existing classification-focused approaches that often yield biased aggregate estimates, our method directly optimizes for unbiased and statistically consistent estimation of document category proportions, even when individual document classification accuracy is low. We demonstrate the utility and robustness of our approach through empirical applications to diverse data sets, including large-scale analysis of political opinions expressed in blogs about the U.S. presidency. The method accommodates investigator-defined categories using a small hand-coded subset and is implemented in freely available software, facilitating scalable and replicable content analysis for social scientists seeking population-level generalizations from textual data.

title: Strategic directions in tissue engineering.
abstract: This study systematically assessed the strategic directions of tissue engineering by engaging 24 global leaders in the field to identify and prioritize critical activity areas necessary for achieving broad clinical success by 2021. Using a modified Hoshin planning process, 145 expert-generated ideas were clustered into 14 key concepts, which were then ranked based on their interrelationships, dominance, and current progress. The analysis revealed a highly interdependent network of priorities, with particular emphasis on angiogenic control, stem cell science, molecular and systems biology, and cell/tissue characterization as immediate focal points. These findings provide a strategic framework to guide research, funding, policy, and development efforts in tissue engineering, aiming to enhance the efficiency and impact of future advancements.
